title: Advertising response redesign (audit E skeptic S5, REDESIGN): the effect of being displayed an advertiser's campaign on the individual's own visit log-odds, identified by Criteo's randomised eligibility (instrumental variable, one-sided non-compliance); prespecified evaluation plan
disclosure: Before this plan was written, one exploratory pass (scratch script, not repository code) computed per-decile exposure rates, ITT, Wald LATE and complier log-odds ratios on the 'explore' rows defined below (10% of the validation split, 279,592 rows). Those rows are excluded from fitting, selection and confirmation. No other validation row and no test row was inspected for this plan.

global_rules.selection: E4: among candidates with compute <= 100 us/row, order by the validation primary metric (ties within 1e-4 to the simpler); keep the first unless its validation long-horizon measure is worse than the smallest one with a paired cluster-bootstrap 95% interval of the difference entirely above 0; keep a simple baseline instead if it is strictly better on test. Here 'validation' is the select split below and no candidate has a long-horizon measure (see long_horizon).
global_rules.bootstrap: Poisson bootstrap of the stratum cells (control, displayed, eligible-not-displayed visit counts; users are iid, so cells resampled as Poisson counts approximate resampling users), 200 resamples, seed 0
global_rules.test_once: the test split is evaluated once, after selection; nothing is refitted afterwards

ad_exposure_response.estimand: the complier effect of being displayed an advertiser's campaign during the test period on the log-odds of visiting the advertiser, as a function of the displayed individual's organic (no-ad) visit log-odds. Identified by the randomised eligibility (treatment) as an instrument for display (exposure): exclusion restriction (eligible users who were never displayed are unaffected) and one-sided non-compliance (no control user is displayed; checked in the conversion record: exposed_in_control = 0)
ad_exposure_response.rows: treated (eligible) users who were displayed the campaign (exposure = 1); target: visit

splits.score: commercial_response@1's kept candidate (t_gbdt_reg), sub-model visit_control, fitted on the train split only: p0_hat(x) is the predicted control-arm visit probability from the 12 anonymised pre-treatment features; it defines strata only
splits.explore: validation rows whose rank r (0-based position in the ascending list of validation row indices of criteo.splits()) has r % 10 == 0; inspected before this plan; excluded from everything below
splits.fit: validation rows with r % 10 in {1, 3, 5, 7, 9} (val-A): stratum edges, nuisance rates and candidate parameters
splits.validation: validation rows with r % 10 in {2, 4, 6, 8} (val-B): selection
splits.test: the whole test split of criteo.splits() (2,795,919 users): confirmation, once

ad_exposure_response.strata: 10 equal-mass bins of p0_hat on the fit split (edges stored); then, from the lowest bin upwards, a bin is merged into its upper neighbour while it has fewer than 300 treated exposed fit rows or its complier baseline moment estimate on the fit split is not strictly inside (0, 1); the top bin is merged downwards under the same condition
ad_exposure_response.nuisance: per split and stratum s, three binomial cells: control (n_c, y_c), eligible displayed (n_te, y_te), eligible never displayed (n_tn, y_tn); e_s = n_te / (n_te + n_tn). Model: never-takers visit with nu_s, compliers' organic (no-ad) visit probability is mu0_s, control visits ~ Bin(n_c, (1 - e_s) nu_s + e_s mu0_s), never-takers ~ Bin(n_tn, nu_s), displayed ~ Bin(n_te, q(mu0_s; theta)). theta (the candidate's effect structure, shared across strata) is fitted on the fit split by maximum likelihood with (nu_s, mu0_s) profiled out. On a held-out split theta is fixed and (nu_s, mu0_s) are re-profiled on that split. For the secondary row-level metrics a displayed row's feature organic_logit = logit of the moment estimate (c_s - (1 - e_s) nu_s) / e_s of its stratum on its own split, clipped to [1e-4, 0.999] (control and never-displayed rows only)
ad_exposure_response.feature_definitions: organic_logit: log-odds of the displayed individual's organic (no-ad) probability of visiting the advertiser in the period. In the data it is the stratum's complier baseline (nuisance above); in the simulator it is the individual's own organic visit probability from the world's discovery mechanism

candidates.B0_no_effect: baseline: q = mu0 (display has no effect on visit)
candidates.B1_constant_difference: baseline and simulator rule: q = clip(mu0 + delta, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6), one delta >= 0 (joint maximum likelihood): the constant absolute effect the runtime served for ad_response@1 (E3 review: constant-effect contender), re-expressed per displayed individual
candidates.M1_constant_log_odds: q = sigmoid(logit mu0 + D), one shift D >= 0 (joint maximum likelihood)
candidates.M2_linear_log_odds: q = sigmoid(logit mu0 + max(a + b (logit mu0 - c), 0)), c = displayed-weighted mean of the moment organic_logit on the fit split (fixed before fitting), (a, b) joint maximum likelihood

ad_exposure_response.negative_effects: every candidate's shift (and B1's difference) is constrained to >= 0 in fitting and serving: no negative persuasion. The report states, per stratum, the test-split 95% bootstrap interval of the unconstrained (saturated) stratum shift; if any interval lies entirely below 0 the constraint is recorded as a known deviation from the data
reported: per-stratum table on fit, validation and test: rows, exposure rate, control rate, never-taker rate, complier baseline, ITT, Wald LATE, unconstrained complier log-odds shift
per-stratum ITT implied by each candidate (e_s (q_s - mu0_s)) against the observed ITT, weighted mean squared error on test

incremental-visit conversion ratio rho = (ITT_conversion / ITT_visit) / (control conversion rate / control visit rate), pooled, with a 95% bootstrap interval on the fit split and on test; the runtime serves the fit estimate when its interval excludes 1, else 1
the conversion analogue of the per-stratum table (complier conversion baseline and shift), descriptive only
95% bootstrap intervals (Poisson cell bootstrap of the fit split, 200 resamples) of the kept candidate's parameters
ad_exposure_response.long_horizon: not applicable: the data have no timestamps; each row is one user over one test period, so repeated campaigns, carry-over, wear-in and wear-out are not identified (recorded as limits). Every candidate's long-horizon measure is null and the E4 drift rule does not reject any candidate
ad_exposure_response.rule_mapping: Simulator rules for display-ad response compared on test on the per-stratum ITT (weighted mean squared error between predicted and observed ITT_s): S1 = runtime ad_response@1 as served (one absolute ITT for every eligible individual); S2 = ad_response@1's prespecified response-type table (model estimate), ITT_s = mean over the stratum's test rows of their assigned type's p1_visit - p0_visit. economy.work's sponsored-search click rule (one hand-set probability) answers a different question (a click on a search result) and has no randomised counterpart in these data: not comparable, stated
ad_exposure_response.serving: runtime decision model ad_response@2: P(visit | campaign displays in the period) = p0 + (A / A_ref) (sigmoid(logit p0 + D(logit p0)) - p0), capped at 1, where p0 is the individual's organic visit probability (world state), A the probability that at least one of the individual's displays in the period is attended, from a registered attention decision model evaluated on each display's own features (relevance, repetition, familiarity) and A_ref = 1 by declaration (a Criteo display is treated as an attended exposure, which understates the effect of an attended display: conservative). The attention composition and A_ref are assumptions, not estimates from these data, and have their own fidelity record. Conversion after a visit is the world's own price-dependent purchase decision; visits the display caused (coupled draw: u in [p0, p)) convert with that decision's probability times rho
ad_exposure_response.compute: evaluation of every candidate is a closed form per row; timed on 100,000 validation rows like the E4 models
ad_exposure_response.primary_metric_definition: (saturated log-likelihood - profile log-likelihood of the candidate with theta fixed) of the split's three cells summed over strata, divided by the split's displayed rows; 0 = the three cell rates of every stratum are reproduced exactly; lower is better
ad_exposure_response.secondary_metric_definition: binary metrics of visit on the split's displayed rows with q evaluated at the rows' moment organic_logit

revision: Revised on 2026-11-26 before any fit on real data (no fit, validation or test row other than the disclosed explore rows had been read): a synthetic randomised trial with a known display shift (tests/test_v5_calibration_ad_exposure.py) showed that plugging the moment estimate of each stratum's complier baseline into the displayed rows' likelihood as if it were known biases the shift towards 0 (errors in variables; 0.89 for a true 1.2 while an oracle baseline gives 1.18). The estimator is therefore the joint three-arm likelihood with the nuisances profiled out, and the primary metric is the held-out profile likelihood. The per-stratum step candidate M3 is dropped (saturated under this likelihood). The first version is in git history (commit 246bea5).
